title: Momoweta Pond (Laurel Lake)
summary: Momoweta Pond, now known as Laurel Lake, is a North Fork waterbody named for Momoweta, sachem of Corchaug.
address_label: Laurel Lake, Laurel / Mattituck, Southold, NY
introduction_content: Momoweta Pond is the historical name connected with modern Laurel Lake near Mattituck and Laurel. The name preserves the memory of Momoweta, sachem of Corchaug, whose leadership appears in several early colonial accounts.
history_content: Momoweta Pond connects modern Laurel Lake with Corchaug leadership context and related name forms. Dated documentary details appear in the Historic Timeline with their own sources.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Momoweta, Moughmaitow, Mowmetow, and Mamawichtouw. The name is interpreted as "he gathereth or brings together in his house," from elements meaning to gather and house.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names have enormous significance in Aboriginal society and culture. As in all societies, they signal the meanings people attach to places, they encode history and geography, they are way-finding devices and common knowledge.”

— Grace Karskens, How a long-lost list is helping us remap Darug place names and culture on Dyarubbin, the Hawkesbury River (2020), article text
whereintheworld_content: The blue marker is an approximate general point for modern Laurel Lake, historically associated with Momoweta Pond in the Mattituck and Laurel area. It does not claim to mark an exact historic boundary or shoreline.
